title: Data residency & region pinning - security review
summary: Customer is evaluating Redwood for regulated EU/US workloads. Primary concerns: region pinning, cross-border processing, sub-processors, KMS integrations, audit logs retention, and SOC 2/ISO evidence. Redwood AE/SE explained Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options, region pinning capabilities, and KMS/HSM patterns. Action: share SOC2 report, processor list, region pinning design doc, and schedule pilot for region-pinned endpoints.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header: Recorded at 2025-05-06T15:00:00Z (UTC) | Duration: 48 min
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Michael Torres (CISO, Acme Financial), Aisha Rahman (Head of Cloud), Luca Moretti (Legal), Katrina Cho (Platform Engineer)

[00:00:05] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro - I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood account, Priya is our SE. Thanks for carving out time for the security deep dive.
[00:00:18] Michael: Hi, Jordan. Appreciate it. We're trying to validate data residency guarantees and understand cross-border handling. We've got EU client data so residency and sub-processors are top of mind.
[00:00:30] Priya: Great. We'll walk through how Redwood supports region pinning and the options for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, and then dig into KMS and audit logs. Quick question: is the goal strict data residency (no cross-border) or just need control over where processing happens?
[00:00:45] Michael: We need EU processing for PII by default — any data that is EU-personal must stay in EU. For some products we might allow processing in US with explicit consent, but core transaction logs must stay in EU. Also need vendor disclosure and SOC 2 evidence.
[00:01:10] Priya: Understood. Quick architecture note: Redwood offers region-pinned endpoints — you can provision model endpoints in eu-west-1 and us-east-1. For Hosted customers we do region pinning at the route level; requests routed to the pinned region, and data stores (logs, KV cache) are colocated. For Dedicated you get a GPU pool in the region you choose; Private gives you the full control.
[00:01:40] Aisha: When you say "Hosted region pinning", what about backups and failover? Is there any automatic cross-region replication for DR that might move data?
[00:01:52] Priya: Good callout. For Hosted, primary processing and short-term cache are kept in the pinned region. We have optional cross-region DR which is off by default for region-pinned setups; turning on DR will replicate snapshots to our DR region — that's a configurable setting and we surface it in the console. For customers with strict residency, we recommend Dedicated or Private with DR disabled or run DR in the same legal jurisdiction.
[00:02:20] Luca: From legal perspective we need the subprocessors list and contractual guarantees. Do you provide a sub-processor registry? How often is it updated?
[00:02:30] Jordan: Yes — we maintain a sub-processor list and a written processor addendum. We'll share the current list; it's updated monthly and we notify customers of material changes.
[00:02:42] Michael: Also encryption. We need to know if Redwood can integrate with our KMS — we use AWS KMS with CMKs and have requirements for key rotation and access controls.
[00:02:55] Priya: We support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private — AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations for on-prem. For Hosted, we offer an option for bring-your-own-KMS in certain enterprise plans where the customer can provide a key and we encrypt stored artifacts with that CMK. For runtime in-memory model tokens are ephemeral and not stored, but logs and embeddings can be encrypted at rest with your key.
[00:03:20] Katrina: You mentioned embeddings — are embeddings persisted in EU if we pin region? We use embeddings for search and must ensure they never leave jurisdiction.
[00:03:31] Priya: Yes, embeddings stored by Redwood for customers with region pinning are persisted in the pinned region. There's a configuration flag in the console: persist_embeddings=true/false and a region checkbox. I'll show a screenshot in the follow-up.
[00:03:50] Michael: What about telemetry and audit logs? We need immutable audit logs for admin actions and access, retained for 7 years for certain regs.
[00:04:02] Priya: Our audit logs include admin API calls, configuration changes, and access events. For Hosted we retain logs for 90 days by default; extended retention is an add-on and can be configured up to multi-year retention. For Dedicated and Private you control retention and can ship logs to your SIEM (we support SQS/Syslog/CloudWatch/Stackdriver). For immutability we can write to WORM storage or transfer to customer-controlled S3 with object lock for compliance scenarios.
[00:04:40] Michael: How are SSO and RBAC handled? We need role separation and SCIM provisioning.
[00:04:48] Jordan: We support SSO via SAML/OIDC and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is role-based with admin, operator, auditor roles; you can limit route-level access. For Dedicated/Private you can push trace logs to your own logging pipeline.
[00:05:05] Aisha: Any concerns about cross-border processing due to sub-processors located in US? For example, some GPUs or inference services might be in US even though the API endpoint is EU.
[00:05:19] Priya: We try to align infra and sub-processors to the region. For Hosted, some sub-services (metrics, billing) may be centralized and could process metadata in US. We keep PII and model data in the pinned region, but metadata could be processed elsewhere — customers with strict requirements often choose Dedicated or Private where we can avoid those cross-border paths. We'll flag any sub-processor that processes customer data outside the pinned region.
[00:05:50] Michael: We need written confirmation that customer PII will not be transferred outside EU for pinned endpoints unless we opt in. Is that a standard contractual term?
[00:05:58] Jordan: Yes we can include that in the DPA/Processor Addendum. Our standard DPA supports region restrictions; for enterprise we add explicit clauses covering non-transfers without consent.
[00:06:12] [00:06:12] (short crosstalk)
[00:06:20] Priya: Quick technical note on KV cache and prefixes — Redis and KV caches are region-local when pinned. There are occasional mis-ops where customers configure global caches; we can enforce region-only caches via policy. Also note that for performance we use prefix caching and sometimes people call it K-V cash in docs, apologies for the typo.
[00:06:45] Katrina: Regarding keys, what's the separation between keys for storage vs keys for transport? TLS is mandatory?
[00:06:52] Priya: TLS 1.2+ for all in-transit. At rest we use envelope encryption — data is encrypted with a data key, which is wrapped by your CMK if provided. For full control we can integrate with HSM-backed KMS in Private deployments.
[00:07:12] Luca: On subprocessors, does Redwood publish SOC 2 or ISO attestations per region? We need to show auditors the certs and scope.
[00:07:23] Jordan: We are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. We'll share the reports under an NDA. The SOC 2 scope covers our core inference platform; we can provide a scope description indicating regions included.
[00:07:40] Michael: Who are your subprocessors for model hosting and telemetry? Any US-based companies we need to flag?
[00:07:48] Jordan: The current subprocessor list includes cloud infra providers (AWS, GCP), analytics providers, and a managed logging provider. We'll share the list; for EU pinned workloads many infra sub-processors operate regionally, but some centralized services may be US-based.
[00:08:05] Aisha: On cross-border legal basis — would Redwood sign a standard SCC / EU addendum?
[00:08:12] Jordan: Yes we support SCCs and will include the relevant EU clauses in the DPA. For Dedicated/Private deployments there's typically no cross-border transfer unless you opt in for backups or DR.
[00:08:25] Katrina: If we do Dedicated in eu-west-1, what's the timeline to provision? We need to do a pilot by end of June.
[00:08:33] Priya: Provisioning Dedicated capacity is typically 2-4 weeks depending on GPU availability; for pilots we often allocate a shared dedicated pool (soft-pool) which can be faster, 1-2 weeks. Private on-prem takes longer due to onboarding.
[00:08:47] Michael: For the pilot we need region-pinned endpoints, CMK integration, and audit logs shipped to our SIEM. Can Redwood deliver that in a pilot?
[00:08:56] Priya: Yes — pilot scope is doable. We'll propose: one region-pinned endpoint in eu-west-1, KMS integration with AWS CMK, and log export to your CloudWatch/Splunk. We'll run a short smoke test and provide runbooks.
[00:09:15] Luca: We'll also require redteam / pen test results or a timeline for third-party tests.
[00:09:22] Jordan: We run annual pen tests and can share results under NDA. We also do regular vulnerability scans.
[00:09:30] [00:09:30] (brief pause)
[00:09:40] Priya: A few subtle items: model weights — are you hosting private models or using public models? Private model hosting has additional IP controls. If you're using open models on Hosted, we still provide the same region pinning but there are different licensing considerations.
[00:09:58] Aisha: We'll likely use a mix — some in-house models for sensitive PII pipelines and public models for generic features.
[00:10:08] Priya: For in-house models we recommend Dedicated or Private so you can control image registries and storage. For public models Hosted is simpler.
[00:10:20] Michael: On audit logs, can we get an immutable chain for admin actions? We need a tamper-evident trail for audits.
[00:10:29] Priya: We can provide signed log exports and support object lock on S3 for immutability. Also can integrate with your audit ledger if you provide an endpoint.
[00:10:45] Katrina: What about sub-processors doing model evaluation, e.g., human-in-the-loop vendors? That would be a showstopper if they are cross-border.
[00:10:56] Jordan: We restrict human review for PII by default; any human review workflow is opt-in and documented in the DPA. We can ensure any human reviewers are in the same jurisdiction or anonymize data first.
[00:11:15] Michael: Good. Now, a couple of clarifying objections: 1) Cost difference between Dedicated and Hosted, and 2) risk of metadata leakage.
[00:11:26] Jordan: Cost wise Hosted is usage-based and typically lower TCO for variable workloads; Dedicated is reserved capacity (commit) and gives better latency and region guarantees. For metadata leakage — we can segregate metadata pipelines, and for strict customers we recommend Dedicated/Private with controlled telemetry endpoints.
[00:11:48] Aisha: From a data residency point, if you ship logs to our SIEM in EU, are there any identifiers in the logs that could reference US zones?
[00:11:58] Priya: Logs include region identifiers but we can scrub or transform certain metadata fields before export if required. We can also route logs through EU endpoints only.
[00:12:12] Michael: Could you walk through a concrete flow for a request: client (EU) -> Redwood endpoint (eu-west-1) -> model inference -> embeddings stored? We want to see all hops.
[00:12:24] Priya: Sure. High level: request hits our edge in eu-west-1 -> routed to region-pinned inference fleet in eu-west-1 -> KV cache in eu-west-1 (Redis) -> transient model artifacts in local SSDs -> response returned. If you enable persistence, embeddings are stored in eu-west-1 S3; audit logs generated in-region and optionally exported. Background analytics may touch regional analytics pipelines; we can opt-out for your account.
[00:12:54] Luca: Any chance of model telemetry (metrics) going to third-party analytics in US?
[00:13:01] Priya: By default metrics are aggregated regionally, but some analytics providers in our stack are centralized. For enterprise accounts we offer a dedicated telemetry pipeline or the ability to stream metrics to your endpoints.
[00:13:15] Michael: On legal standing, do you accept contractual restrictions that prevent Redwood from using certain sub-processors?
[00:13:26] Jordan: In enterprise DPAs we can add restrictions and approval gates for new sub-processors; absolute exclusions are negotiable but may impact functionality. We typically allow customers to opt out of specific processors with a mitigation plan.
[00:13:40] Aisha: For the pilot, we need a checklist and an architecture diagram that shows all data flows and sub-processors.
[00:13:48] Priya: We'll include a region-focused architecture diagram in the follow-up along with the sub-processor registry and a sample DPA with region clauses.
[00:13:59] Michael: Great. Any open issues we haven't covered?
[00:14:05] Luca: Need to confirm retention length options and proof for pen tests and SOC 2 scope.
[00:14:10] Jordan: We'll attach SOC 2 report, pen test summary, sub-processor list, region design doc, and a proposed pilot SOW.
[00:14:22] [00:14:22] (brief background noise)
[00:14:30] Priya: Quick FAQ item — cross-border encryption keys. If you use a CMK in aws-eu, we won't export that key material; for Hosted BYOK we have a key wrapping flow where the CMK never leaves your account. There have been some customers who called it "bring your own K-M-S" and spelled KMS weirdly in notes.
[00:14:55] Katrina: How will changes be communicated if a sub-processor is added that impacts residency?
[00:15:02] Jordan: We'll notify customers 30 days in advance for material changes and provide mitigation options; disclosure is part of the contract.
[00:15:15] Michael: We also need clarity on backups — are backups stored in the same region by default?
[00:15:22] Priya: Backups are stored in-region for region-pinned setups unless you enable cross-region backup. We'll make sure that's documented.
[00:15:33] Aisha: Two small items — are cookies or analytics tags used that ping US endpoints?
[00:15:40] Jordan: Minimal on the platform; most front-end analytics are opt-in. We'll provide a web tracker inventory.
[00:15:52] [00:15:52] (crosstalk)
[00:16:00] Priya: Okay, quick recap: deliverables are SOC 2 report (NDA), current sub-processor list, region pinning design doc, KMS integration guide, sample DPA with region clause, and a pilot SOW for eu-west-1 including CMK and SIEM log export.
[00:16:18] Michael: Timeline? We need pilot by end of June.
[00:16:22] Jordan: We'll aim to have deliverables within 3 business days; pilot provisioning 1-2 weeks for soft Dedicated, 2-4 weeks for reserved Dedicated. If dates align we can target provisioning in the first half of June to start testing.
[00:16:38] Luca: We'll need pricing for Dedicated pilot and any add-on for long-term log retention.
[00:16:44] Jordan: I'll follow up with pricing ranges and a draft SOW.
[00:16:50] [00:16:50] (participants exchange small talk)
[00:17:05] Katrina: One operational question — who will have access to encryption keys in your hosted BYOK flow?
[00:17:12] Priya: You retain control of CMKs; Redwood does not have access to unwrapped key material. We use envelope encryption; Redwood has access to wrapped keys only when needed for customer operations and only under strict RBAC and audit conditions.
[00:17:30] Michael: Any final risk items?
[00:17:34] Jordan: Only that some Hosted sub-services may be centralized; otherwise mitigation via Dedicated/Private and contract language.
[00:17:45] Aisha: Ok thanks, can you send over the artifacts?
[00:17:50] Jordan: Yes. We'll send the SOC 2, sub-processor list, region doc, KMS guide, retention options, and SOW. Also propose a follow-up for June 10 to check pilot readiness.
[00:18:03] Michael: Sounds good.
[00:18:10] [00:18:10] End of main discussion — Q&A continued for another ~30 minutes covering implementation details and minor config settings. Excerpts below.
[00:18:25] [00:19:00] Priya: Implementation excerpt: to pin a route you set "region: eu-west-1" in the route config; we recommend setting "data_residency: true" so logs and KV are forced in-region. Some older SDKs mis-handle the header name, watch for that.
[00:20:05] Katrina: Does the SDK transmit headers that might accidentally route to US?
[00:20:12] Priya: New SDKs are safe; older internal builds might default to global endpoints. We'll share the verification tests.
[00:22:30] Michael: For the pilot, can you provide a runbook for failover tests and prove that failover can be disabled?
[00:22:38] Priya: Yes — failover is a toggle. We'll include a short runbook for failover disable and re-enable.
[00:25:00] [00:25:00] (technical deep dive by Priya on KMS integration, 15 minutes - details omitted in transcript extract)
[00:40:00] Priya: Summary of KMS integration steps: enroll account in BYOK, configure key policy to allow Redwood service principal to wrap/unwrap but not export, set key rotation to your policy, test by encrypting a sample S3 object in eu-west-1.
[00:41:10] Michael: We'll need proof that Redwood's service principal cannot exfiltrate keys.
[00:41:20] Priya: For Dedicated/Private, the CMK resides in your account; for Hosted BYOK we do a wrap-only flow — we'll provide a security design doc showing the flow.
[00:42:05] Priya: Final operational notes: telemetry can be shunted to your EU telemetry pipeline and we can disable centralized analytics per-account.
[00:42:30] Jordan: Next steps recap coming up.
[00:42:40] [00:42:40] (wrap up)
[00:43:00] Jordan: Thanks all. We'll follow up within 3 business days with artifacts and a proposed pilot SOW. Proposed follow-up meeting June 10.
[00:43:12] Michael: Thanks, talk soon.
[00:47:30] (call ended)

Notes on transcription quality: some names and acronyms may be slightly off (e.g., K-V cache vs KV cache, K-M-S vs KMS).
